en: first lady; honorific for a distinguished person's wife

examples.en: The president and the first lady attended the event together.

examples.ko: 영부인은 어려운 이웃을 직접 만나 위로했어요.
examples.en: The first lady met neighbors in need in person and comforted them.

examples.ko: 외국 정상의 영부인을 초대해 점심을 대접했어요.
examples.en: They invited a foreign leader's wife and treated her to lunch.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 영부인의 해외 방문 소식이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news reported on the first lady's overseas visit.
The first lady kindly wrote a letter herself.

examples.ko: 미국 영부인이 어린이 교육에 관심이 많았대요.
examples.en: I heard the American first lady was very interested in children's education.

explain: 원래는 지위가 높은 사람의 아내를 높여 부르는 말인데, 요즘은 주로 대통령의 아내를 가리켜요. 자기 아내에게는 쓰지 않고, 일반 사람의 아내는 '부인', '사모님'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: The president's wife visited the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영부인 앞에 누구의 아내인지 밝히는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, making clear whose wife is meant.

phrases.en: The First Lady attended the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높이는 말이라서 주어 뒤에 '께서'를 붙이고 서술어에도 '-시-'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is honorific, 께서 follows the subject and the verb takes -시-.

phrases.example: 그 나라의 퍼스트레이디는 책을 많이 읽는 것으로 유명해요.
phrases.en: That country's first lady is famous for reading a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영어에서 온 말로 영부인과 같은 뜻이고, 뉴스나 잡지에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword from English meaning the same as 영부인, common in news and magazines.

explain_en: Originally an honorific for the wife of a person of high standing, it now mostly refers to a president's wife. You never use it for your own wife; for other people's wives you say '부인' or '사모님'.

examples.en: The company treats retired seniors with proper respect.

examples.ko: 손님을 예우하는 마음으로 음식을 정성껏 준비했어요.
examples.en: I prepared the food with care, treating the guests with due honor.

examples.ko: 나라를 위해 일한 분들을 예우해야 해요.
examples.en: We should honor the people who worked for the country.

examples.ko: 대회 우승자를 최고로 예우해서 특별 좌석을 마련했어요.
examples.en: They honored the winner as the top guest and prepared a special seat.
I gave up my seat to show respect to the elderly person.
The school decided to honor the teacher who retired.

explain: 사람의 지위나 공로에 맞게 높여서 대접한다는 느낌이에요. '대접하다'보다 격식 있는 말투이고, 명사로 '예우를 받다', '예우를 갖추다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: He was treated with honor as a state guest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예우하다'를 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person being treated respectfully.

phrases.en: We treated our retired senior colleague with proper respect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격식과 예의를 맞춰 대한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to show proper formality and courtesy.

phrases.en: I treated the guest with the greatest respect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높일 사람에게 '-아/어 드리다'를 붙여 공손하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 드리다' makes it polite toward the person honored.

explain_en: It carries the feel of treating a person with respect that fits their position or merit. It is more formal than '대접하다', and the noun is often used as '예우를 받다' (be treated with respect) or '예우를 갖추다' (show proper respect).

en: to be affable; to be mild; to be gentle

examples.ko: 우리 교수님은 성품이 온후해서 학생들이 잘 따라요.
examples.en: Our professor has a gentle character, so the students follow him well.

examples.ko: 온후한 미소를 가진 할아버지가 문을 열어 주셨어요.
examples.en: An old man with a kindly smile opened the door for us.
He treats everyone with kindness.
The boss looks mild, but he is thorough about work.
He is a person the word 'gentle' suits well.
I still remember his gentle appearance.

explain: 사람의 성품이나 표정이 따뜻하고 너그러울 때 써요. 어른이나 존경하는 분에게 어울리는 격식 있는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '다정하다'나 '착하다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The teacher is famous for a gentle character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성품을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for praising someone's character.

phrases.en: My grandfather is really gentle and kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게 높임으로 쓸 때의 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for an elder.

phrases.en: The new teacher is warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: '온후하다'보다 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday word than 온후하다.

explain_en: It is used when a person's character or expression is warm and generous. It is a formal word that suits elders or people you respect, while in daily talk people more often say '다정하다' or '착하다'.

examples.en: My younger sister got married, so I now have a brother-in-law.

examples.ko: 제부도 우리 가족 모임에 올 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard my sister's husband can come to our family gathering too.
On the weekend I went fishing with my sister's husband.
Yesterday I got a birthday present from my sister's husband.
I asked my sister's husband to look after the child.

examples.ko: 동생과 제부는 서울에 살고 저는 부산에 살아요.
examples.en: My sister and her husband live in Seoul and I live in Busan.

explain: 여자가 여동생의 남편을 부르거나 가리키는 말이에요. 남자가 누이동생의 남편을 말할 때는 '매제'라고 하고, 언니의 남편은 '형부'라고 해요. 가족 호칭은 말하는 사람의 성별에 따라 달라져서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.

phrases.example: 이번 주말에 제부와 함께 식사할 거예요.
phrases.en: I'll have a meal with my brother-in-law this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '와'를 붙여 함께 하는 사람으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 와, he becomes the person you do something with.

phrases.en: My brother-in-law is really good at cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족을 말할 때 '우리'를 붙여 자연스럽게 소개해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 우리 is the natural way to introduce a family member.

phrases.en: My sister's husband came along too, not just my younger brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제부'는 여자가 쓰고, 남자는 누이동생의 남편을 '매제'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Women say 제부, while men call a younger sister's husband 매제.

explain_en: A woman uses it for her younger sister's husband. A man calls his younger sister's husband '매제', and a woman calls her older sister's husband '형부'. Family terms change depending on the speaker's gender, so they are easy to mix up.

examples.ko: 조교수님이 이번 학기 수업을 맡게 되셨어요.
examples.en: The assistant professor will teach this semester's class.
I became an assistant professor at a university this year.

examples.ko: 김 조교수는 연구실에서 논문을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: Assistant Professor Kim is writing a paper in the lab.
You need a doctorate to become an assistant professor.
The students asked the assistant professor a lot of questions.
That assistant professor is very popular with students.

explain: 대학교 교수 직급은 보통 조교수, 부교수, 교수 순서로 올라가요. 직접 부를 때는 '조교수님'보다 그냥 '교수님'이라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아요. '조교'는 수업을 돕는 사람이라 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I asked the assistant professor a question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직급을 말하며 높여 부를 때 써요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '교수님'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer respectfully to the rank; to address them directly, people usually say '교수님'.

phrases.en: Next year I'll be promoted from assistant professor to associate professor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조교수 다음 직급이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The rank right above 조교수.

phrases.en: Professor, I have a question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부를 때는 직급에 관계없이 '교수님'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When addressing someone directly, use '교수님' regardless of rank.

explain_en: University ranks usually go 조교수, 부교수, 교수. When addressing someone directly, people far more often just say 교수님. Note that 조교 is a teaching assistant, which is a different thing.

en: mid-level; established (core member of a field); mid-sized

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원 수가 많은 중견 기업이에요.
examples.en: That company is a mid-sized firm with many employees.
As a seasoned actor, he takes good care of his juniors.

examples.ko: 저는 대기업보다 중견 기업에서 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work at a mid-sized company rather than a big corporation.

examples.ko: 중견 작가의 새 소설이 이번 주에 나와요.
examples.en: A new novel by an established writer comes out this week.
The mid-career staff are the busiest on the team.

examples.ko: 그는 이제 업계의 중견으로 인정받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is now recognized as an established figure in the industry.

explain: 신입도 아니고 원로도 아닌, 한 분야에서 중심을 잡고 있는 믿을 만한 사람을 가리켜요. '중견 기업'은 대기업과 중소기업의 중간 규모 회사를 말하고, '중견 배우', '중견 작가'처럼 자주 써요. 새로 나온 사람을 말하는 '신예'와 대비해서 외워 두세요.

phrases.example: 저는 직원이 오백 명쯤 되는 중견 기업에 다녀요.
phrases.en: I work at a mid-sized company with about five hundred employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대기업과 중소기업의 중간 규모 회사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a company between a large corporation and a small business.

phrases.example: 그 중견 배우는 어떤 역할도 잘해요.
phrases.en: That veteran actor plays any role well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경력이 쌓여 믿을 만한 배우를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes an experienced actor you can rely on.

phrases.example: 중견 작가의 새 소설이 다음 달에 나와요.
phrases.en: The new novel by an established writer comes out next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신인은 아니고 한 분야에서 자리를 잡은 작가를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a writer who is no longer a newcomer and has an established place in the field.

explain_en: It points to a reliable person who is neither a newcomer nor a senior elder, but is carrying a field. '중견 기업' means a company between large and small ones, and it is often used as in '중견 배우' and '중견 작가'. Remember it in contrast with '신예', which means a newcomer.

examples.en: My father rose to lieutenant colonel in the army.
The lieutenant colonel gave a greeting in front of the unit.
That lieutenant colonel is kind to his men.
My uncle will soon be promoted to lieutenant colonel.

examples.ko: 영화에서 중령 역할을 맡은 배우가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The actor who played the lieutenant colonel in the movie was cool.
Above lieutenant colonel there is colonel.

explain: 군대 계급이에요. 소령 위, 대령 아래예요. 부를 때는 이름이나 계급 뒤에 '님'을 붙여 '중령님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The lieutenant colonel will come to the unit tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 부르거나 높여 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 when addressing or speaking respectfully about the officer.

phrases.en: My uncle was promoted to lieutenant colonel this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계급이 올라갈 때 '○○으로 진급하다'라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '○○으로 진급하다' when someone moves up in rank.
phrases.en_equiv: to be promoted to lieutenant colonel

phrases.en: My grandfather was a reserve lieutenant colonel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대를 떠난 사람의 계급을 말할 때 앞에 '예비역'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 예비역 in front when talking about the rank of someone who has left active service.

explain_en: A military rank, above 소령 (major) and below 대령 (colonel). When addressing the person, add '님' and say '중령님'.

examples.ko: 호텔 지배인이 직접 방을 안내해 줬어요.
examples.en: The hotel manager showed us to the room himself.
If there's a problem, please call the manager.
The restaurant manager apologized to the customer.

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 호텔에서 일해서 지배인이 됐어요.
examples.en: I worked at a hotel for ten years and became the manager.
The manager looks after the staff's schedules.

examples.ko: 예약이 안 되어 있어서 지배인과 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The reservation wasn't made, so I talked with the manager.

explain: '지배인'은 호텔, 식당, 극장 같은 곳에서 가게 일을 맡아 관리하는 사람이에요. 가게의 주인은 '사장'이나 '업주'이고, '지배인'은 주인 대신 일하는 사람이에요. 회사의 관리자는 '부장', '팀장'이라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 식당 지배인이 예약 문제를 해결해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The restaurant manager solved the reservation problem for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지배인' 앞에 장소를 붙여 어디의 지배인인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the place before 지배인 to say where the manager works.

phrases.en: Manager, may I speak with you for a moment?
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부를 때 '님'을 붙이면 공손해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 님 makes it polite when addressing the manager directly.

phrases.en: If there's a problem with your room, please ask the manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호텔이나 식당에서 문제가 있을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is a problem at a hotel or restaurant.

explain_en: '지배인' runs the daily operation of a hotel, restaurant, or theater. The owner is the '사장' or '업주', while the '지배인' works on their behalf. Managers in a company are called '부장' or '팀장'.

examples.en: The branch manager went on a business trip to headquarters today.
Our branch manager is changing next month.
He was promoted to branch manager in Seoul.
We have to report to the branch manager first.
There is a company dinner to welcome the new branch manager.

examples.ko: 지사장과 본사 임원이 회의를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The branch manager and a head-office executive are in a meeting.

explain: 본사에 대한 지사, 곧 지역 사무소의 책임자를 말해요. 직함이라서 말할 때는 '지사장님'으로 높여 불러요. 은행이나 가게의 분점 책임자는 보통 '지점장'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I reported to the branch manager first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직함 뒤에 '님'을 붙여 높여 부르거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '님' to the title is the respectful way to address or mention the person.

phrases.en: He works as an overseas branch manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본사가 아닌 다른 나라의 사무소를 책임진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the head of an office in another country, not the headquarters.

phrases.en: I met the bank branch manager.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지사장'은 지역 사무소, '지점장'은 은행이나 가게의 분점 책임자예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '지사장' heads a regional office, while '지점장' heads a bank or store branch.

explain_en: It refers to the head of a branch office as opposed to the head office. Because it is a job title, people address the person as '지사장님' to show respect. The head of a bank or shop branch is usually called '지점장'.

examples.ko: 팀장님은 실수를 숨긴 직원을 크게 질책했어요.
examples.en: The team leader sharply reprimanded the employee who hid a mistake.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아이를 질책하기보다 이유를 먼저 물어보셨어요.
examples.en: Rather than scolding the child, his parents asked the reason first.

examples.ko: 감독은 경기 후에 선수들을 질책하지 않고 격려했어요.
examples.en: After the game, the coach encouraged the players instead of rebuking them.

examples.ko: 언론이 정부의 늦은 대응을 질책하고 있어요.
examples.en: The press is criticizing the government's slow response.

examples.ko: 스스로를 질책하며 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I blamed myself and couldn't sleep all night.

examples.ko: 선배에게 질책을 받을까 봐 보고하기가 무서웠어요.
examples.en: I was afraid to report because I might get rebuked by my senior.

explain: '혼내다', '야단치다'는 구어체이고, '질책하다'는 좀 더 격식 있는 말이에요. 윗사람이 잘못을 꾸짖을 때나 뉴스에서 비판할 때 많이 써요. 윗사람이 한 일에는 '질책하셨어요'처럼 높여요.

phrases.en: I was reprimanded by my team leader because of a mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질책을 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때는 '질책을 받다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this from the point of view of the person being reprimanded.

phrases.en: The president rebuked the employee who broke a promise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 한 일이라서 높임 '-시-'를 넣은 존댓말 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific '-시-' form, used when a superior does the reprimanding.

phrases.en: The teacher sternly rebuked the student who lied.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄하게'를 붙이면 강하게 꾸짖는 정도를 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '엄하게' shows how harsh the rebuke is.

explain_en: '혼내다' and '야단치다' are colloquial, while '질책하다' is more formal. It is common when a superior scolds someone for a fault or when the news criticizes something. For a superior's action, honorify it as '질책하셨어요'.

examples.en: The general was appointed commander-in-chief of the whole army.
The supreme commander visited the front line in person.

examples.ko: 역사 영화에서 총사령관은 늘 지도를 보고 있어요.
examples.en: In historical movies, the commander-in-chief is always looking at a map.
In this game, I'm the supreme commander.
All the units moved on the commander-in-chief's order.

examples.ko: 새 총사령관을 누구로 뽑을지 논의 중이에요.
examples.en: They are discussing who to choose as the new commander-in-chief.

explain: 군 전체를 이끄는 가장 높은 지휘관을 말해요. '사령관'은 한 부대의 지휘관도 되지만 '총사령관'은 전체를 맡는다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: That general was appointed supreme commander.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리를 맡길 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Collocation for being given the post.

phrases.en: Everyone followed the commander-in-chief's order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 높은 지휘관의 명령을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the top commander's orders.

phrases.en: The commander visited the unit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '총사령관'보다 범위가 좁을 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: May cover a narrower scope than 총사령관.

explain_en: It refers to the top commander who leads the entire military. A '사령관' can command a single unit, while a '총사령관' is in charge of everything.

examples.en: He earned the title 'the nation's singer'.
You should use the correct title for your teacher.
The title 'hero of the World Cup' was attached to that player.
This title isn't given to just anyone.
Is it okay to call him by name only, without a title?
They give the champion title to the winner of the contest.

explain: '사장님', '박사'처럼 이름 앞뒤에 붙이는 말이나, 업적 때문에 붙은 이름(국민 가수)을 가리켜요. '호칭'은 사람을 부르는 말에 초점이 있고, 칭호는 지위나 명예를 나타내는 이름에 많이 써요. '칭호를 얻다/받다/붙다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The school gave him an honorary title.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업적을 인정해서 주는 영예로운 이름을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an honorable title given to recognize achievements.

phrases.en: Fans gave him the title 'fairy.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 별명 같은 이름을 붙여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving someone a nickname-like title.

phrases.en: At work, we decide on how to address each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '칭호'는 지위나 명예의 이름이고, '호칭'은 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 칭호 is a title of status or honor; 호칭 is a form of address.

explain_en: It refers to a name attached to a person such as '사장님' or '박사', or a name earned through achievements, like '국민 가수'. '호칭' focuses on the word you use to address someone, while 칭호 is often used for a name showing rank or honor. It goes with '칭호를 얻다/받다/붙다'.

dis.h: honorary or official title given to someone

p.n: 타이틀 is more casual and loanword-like; 칭호 sounds formal and official.

examples.en: The team leader directs a team of ten people.

examples.ko: 팀장이 팀원들을 잘 통솔하면 위기 때도 팀이 흔들리지 않아요.
examples.en: If the team leader leads the team well, the team doesn't waver even in a crisis.

examples.ko: 군대에서는 지휘관이 부대를 잘 통솔하는 것이 가장 중요하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the most important thing in the military is for the commander to lead the unit well.

examples.ko: 많은 사람을 통솔하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Leading a large group of people is not easy.
We need someone to take charge of the children at camp.
He wasn't able to lead his subordinates well.

explain: 여러 사람을 하나로 모아 이끈다는 뜻으로, '이끌다'보다 격식 있고 권위가 느껴져요. 학급, 팀, 군대 같은 집단을 대상으로 하고, '통솔력'이라는 말을 특히 많이 써요. 한 사람을 가르치거나 돕는 상황에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: Our class president has leadership ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들을 이끄는 능력을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to talk about the ability to lead people.

phrases.en: The teacher keeps the students well under control and leads them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학급이나 단체를 하나로 이끌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when leading a class or group as one.

phrases.example: 그 선수가 팀을 잘 이끌고 있어요.
phrases.en: That player is leading the team well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, softer word.

explain_en: It means gathering many people together and leading them as one, and it feels more formal and authoritative than '이끌다'. Its object is a group such as a class, team, or army, and the word '통솔력' (leadership) is especially common. It does not fit situations of teaching or helping a single person.

en: ship's captain; commander of a warship

examples.en: The captain gave an order to all the crew.
I thought the captain role I saw in the movie was cool.

examples.ko: 함장은 배가 안전하게 항구에 닿을 때까지 자리를 지켰어요.
examples.en: The captain stayed at his post until the ship safely reached port.
My grandfather was a navy captain when he was young.
Captain, I see a large ship ahead!

examples.ko: 새로 온 함장은 승무원들과 먼저 인사를 나눴어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived captain first greeted the crew.

explain: 함장은 군함의 가장 높은 책임자예요. 일반 배나 여객선의 책임자는 '선장'이라고 해요. 비행기는 '기장'이고 잠수함도 '함장'을 써요.

phrases.en: The captain came out onto the deck.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함장'을 높여 부르거나 직접 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form of 함장, used to address or refer to the captain respectfully.

phrases.en: He is a submarine captain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함장이 어떤 배의 책임자인지 밝힐 때 앞에 배 이름을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the type of vessel before 함장 shows which ship the captain commands.

phrases.example: 그는 십 년 뒤에 함장이 됐어요.
phrases.en: Ten years later, he became a captain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군함의 책임자 자리에 오르는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rising to the position of commanding a warship.

explain_en: A 함장 is the commanding officer of a warship. The person in charge of an ordinary ship or ferry is a 선장, and for an airplane it is 기장. Submarines also use 함장.

examples.en: He was a professor and then came to work as an administrator.

examples.ko: 좋은 행정가는 시민의 말을 잘 들어요.
examples.en: A good administrator listens well to citizens.

examples.ko: 시장은 오랫동안 일한 행정가를 새 부시장으로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: The mayor chose a long-serving administrator as the new deputy mayor.
My father was an administrator who worked at city hall.

examples.ko: 학자와 행정가의 생각은 서로 다를 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Scholars and administrators often think differently.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 행정가가 되어 지역을 돕고 싶어요.
examples.en: Later I want to become an administrator and help my region.

explain: '정치가'는 선거나 정당 활동으로 정치를 하는 사람이고, '행정가'는 정책을 실제로 실행하고 조직을 운영하는 사람이에요. 공무원 전체를 부를 때는 보통 '공무원'이라고 하고, '행정가'는 능력이나 경력을 이야기할 때 써요.

phrases.en: He is known as a capable administrator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing used to praise someone's ability.

phrases.example: 새 시장은 행정가 출신이라서 일 처리가 빨라요.
phrases.en: The new mayor comes from an administrative background, so he gets things done quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 사람의 경력이 행정 분야임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone's career background is in administration.

phrases.en: As an administrator, you have to work with a sense of responsibility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자격이나 입장을 나타낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state someone's role or standpoint.

explain_en: A '정치가' (politician) works in politics through elections or parties, while a '행정가' runs organizations and carries out policy. For public workers in general people usually say '공무원'; '행정가' is used when talking about someone's ability or career.

en: on intimate terms with; without reserve; candidly

examples.en: The staff treat the regular customer in a very friendly way.

examples.ko: 선배가 허물없이 말을 걸어 줘서 편했어요.
examples.en: The senior talked to me so casually that I felt at ease.
We are on very easy, intimate terms with each other.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 누구에게나 허물없이 웃으며 인사해요.
examples.en: That person greets everyone with a warm, open smile.
If you have a worry, please tell me freely.

examples.ko: 처음 보는 사람과도 허물없이 어울리는 게 신기해요.
examples.en: It is amazing how you mix easily even with people you have just met.

explain: '허물없이 대하다·지내다·이야기하다·어울리다'처럼 사람과 관계를 맺는 동사와 함께 써요. 격식 없이 마음을 터놓는 따뜻한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: We have been on easy, close terms for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 가깝고 편하게 지낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for being on close and comfortable terms.

phrases.en: Talking openly with a friend puts my mind at ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨기는 것 없이 편하게 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means talking freely without holding anything back.

phrases.en: All the neighbors mingle easily with one another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 거리낌 없이 함께 지낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people get along together without reserve.

explain_en: It pairs with verbs about relating to people, such as '허물없이 대하다/지내다/이야기하다/어울리다'. It carries a warm feeling of being open and unceremonious.

examples.en: Grandfather shouted orders at the children in a loud voice.
The commander barks at the soldiers to move forward.

examples.ko: 사장님이 직원들을 호령하듯 말해서 분위기가 무거워졌어요.
examples.en: The boss spoke as if giving orders to the staff, and the mood became heavy.

examples.ko: 그는 이 동네를 호령하던 유명한 사람이었어요.
examples.en: He was a famous man who used to rule this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 왕이 신하들에게 호령하는 장면이 드라마에 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in the drama where the king shouts orders at his subjects.

examples.ko: 그렇게 호령하지 말고 부드럽게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't bark orders like that; speak gently.

explain: 힘 있는 사람이 크고 위엄 있게 명령하는 모습에 써요. 화가 나서 크게 야단치는 '호통치다'와 비슷하지만, '호령하다'는 명령하거나 다스리는 느낌이 더 강해요. 사극이나 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 비유로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The general commanded the soldiers in a loud voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위엄 있게 크게 명령하는 모습에 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for commanding loudly and with authority.

phrases.en: That king once ruled over the whole land.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 힘을 가지고 다스리는 모습을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for ruling with great power.

phrases.en: The father scolded his son loudly for coming home late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화가 나서 크게 야단치는 말로, '호령하다'는 명령하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means scolding loudly out of anger; 호령하다 has more of a commanding feel.

explain_en: It describes a powerful person giving orders in a loud, commanding way. It is close to '호통치다' (to scold loudly), but '호령하다' feels more like commanding or ruling. It often appears in historical dramas and stories, and in daily life it is sometimes used figuratively.
